newsitem.title: USA: Shots fired at Calif. plant after McVeigh verdict.
newsitem.headline: Shots fired at Calif. plant after McVeigh verdict.

text.p: An unidentified gunman, apparently upset over the Oklahoma City bombing verdict, fired more than 50 rounds at a power substation in California on Tuesday, authorities said.
No one was injured in the early morning attack, but the bullets knocked out power to homes near the Emerald Lake substation, owned by PG&E Corp.'s Pacific Gas and Electric Co.

Officials said there was evidence the shooting was in response to Monday's conviction in Denver of Timothy McVeigh for setting off the truck bomb that destroyed the federal building in Oklahoma City on April 19, 1995, killing 168 people.

George Berry, a spokesman for the San Mateo County sheriff's department, said authorities found 55 rifle shell casings at the scene, a newspaper bearing the headline "McVeigh Guilty," and a Confederate flag attached to the fence of the substation.
"Originally it was looking like some nut shooting at PG&E, but obviously with the McVeigh angle it changes the investigation," Berry said.
Berry said deputies were searching for the suspect in a park area near the substation, about 25 miles (40 km) south of San Francisco.

Pacific Gas and Electric spokeswoman Mary Rodrigues said the shooting knocked out power to 2,000 of its customers. She said two transformers at the substation were taken out of service because of the damage, estimated at $500,000.
"We found bullets in our transformer," Rodrigues said. "Who knows what they were aiming at."
